validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/SPEC (high, 3 independent sources agree on core specs): (1) Al-Ahram Gate (gate.ahram.org.eg/News/1367155.aspx, 2017-01-03) reports a court case by Suez Cement Co. challenging Petroleum Minister decree 717/2016, a temporary 15-month land seizure for a natural-gas pipeline project 'New Administrative Capital/Dahshour', 70 km long, crossing Cairo and Giza governorates, and names both the EGAS chairman and GASCO chairman as defendants -- confirms length=70km, Cairo/Giza governorates, and EGAS/GASCO institutional involvement. (2) Egypt's Projects Map (egy-map.com), sourced explicitly 'from the official website of the Presidency', titled 'إنشاء خط العاصمة الجديدة - دهشور (سيمينز)' -- gives 32-inch diameter, 70 km length, cost EGP 605 million, completed July 2017, explicit purpose 'to feed the New Administrative Capital's [Siemens] power plant with gas'. Marked 'implemented' (تم تنفيذه). (3) petro-news.com/95212/ ('39 مشروعاً .. خريطة مشروعات القاز الطبيعي في مصر'), an independent bulk survey of 39 Egyptian gas-infrastructure projects, lists this exact project ('New Administrative Capital-Dahshur (Siemens)') as item #20: 32-inch, 70 km, EGP 605 million, feeding the Siemens power station -- matching GEM's Length/Diameter/Cost/purpose exactly. All three independently agree: Length=70km (MATCH), Diameter=32in (MATCH), Cost=EGP 605M (MATCH), StartYear=2017 (MATCH, egy-map dates completion to July 2017). Tier: HIGH (>=2 independent, in fact 3, all agreeing on value).
DUPLICATE CHECK (resolved, no duplicate): The same petro-news.com survey independently lists TWO OTHER, DISTINCT New-Administrative-Capital-power-plant gas supply projects in the same article: item #12 = El Tina-Abu Sultan-New Administrative Capital (42in, 165km, EGP 3.335B, across Cairo/Ismailia/Port Said) = GEM's P3366 (matches exactly: len=165, dia=42); and item #23 = 'New Administrative Capital Power Station Supply Line', described as an EMERGENCY supply line to the Siemens plant, 32in, 63km, EGP 327M = GEM's P7574 'New Administration Capital PS Gas Pipeline' (matches exactly: len=63, dia=32, cost=327M, owner listed there as General Petroleum Co). Despite superficial similarity (both P3930 and P7574 are 32in lines feeding the same Siemens plant), the same independent official-project survey enumerates them as two SEPARATE, differently-costed, differently-routed projects (P3930 apparently the planned/primary trunk from Dahshour, decreed 2016/land dispute 2017, completed 2017; P7574 an 'emergency' supplementary line, later/different owner attribution GPC vs EGAS). No duplicate/relabel concern -- treat as distinct, both real.
CLASSIFICATION: Correctly a gas TRANSMISSION trunk (32in x 70km connecting a national-grid tie-in at Dahshour, Giza, across greater Cairo to a major 4,800 MW combined-cycle power station at the New Administrative Capital) -- not a plant-internal or gathering line. Confirmed.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100% is plausible and partially corroborated -- the Ahram legal notice names both the EGAS chairman and the GASCO ('جاسكو', Egyptian Natural Gas Co) chairman as defendants tied to this specific pipeline, consistent with EGAS as the parent holding company and GASCO as the likely operating subsidiary. Neither of the two GEM sources names EGAS by name directly as owner (that appears to be GEM's own convention/inference for EGAS-holding-company gas trunklines rather than a direct citation), so tag this as medium-tier corroboration for Owner specifically, though the pipeline's existence/specs are high-tier. Recommend adding GASCO as Operator (currently blank) given its explicit naming in the Ahram case.
DATA-QUALITY FLAG (not a spec/existence concern but should be fixed on apply): the sheet's FuelSource cell currently holds the raw egy-map.com URL (https://egy-map.com/project/...) instead of a fuel description like 'Natural gas' -- this looks like the ref URL was pasted into the value cell by mistake. Recommend on apply: FuelSource='Natural gas' (or 'Gas', matching controlled vocab used elsewhere), and move the URL into FuelSource [ref].

routes.start_name: Dahshur gas tie-in/distribution point, Giza Governorate (GASCO national-grid hub near Dahshur town, corridor shared with the South Valley Gas Pipeline and Dahshur–Mostorod line)
routes.end_name: New Administrative Capital – Siemens combined-cycle power plant supply zone, Cairo Governorate (New Capital 'power plant zone', east of the New Capital's downtown/government district along the Katameya–Ain Sokhna corridor)

waypoints.name: El Katameya (New Cairo), Cairo Governorate -- confirmed waypoint: Al-Ahram's 2017 court report states the decreed route runs 'in front of' Suez Cement Co.'s factory at Qattamiya

routes.corridor_desc: Al-Ahram's court report (decree 717/2016) places the route across Cairo and Giza governorates and explicitly names El Katameya (Qattamiya), southeast Cairo along the Cairo–Ain Sokhna corridor, as a point the line passes through/near (it runs in front of Suez Cement's Katameya plant, which triggered the land-seizure dispute). Egy-map/Presidency source confirms the line's purpose is to feed the New Administrative Capital's Siemens power station, sited ~42km east of Cairo off the Katameya–Ain Sokhna road. Combined with the pipeline name itself ('New Administrative Capital–Dahshur'), the most defensible corridor is: Dahshur (Giza, west bank GASCO grid tie-in) -> crosses the Nile/greater Cairo southern periphery -> El Katameya/Ain Sokhna Road corridor (confirmed waypoint) -> New Administrative Capital power-plant zone. I could not independently source the power plant's exact coordinates (no official lat/lon published in the sources checked), so the eastern endpoint given is the New Capital's general downtown/government-district coordinate, not the precise plant gate -- treat it as an approximate anchor, not a precise tie-in point. Start/waypoint coordinates are standard, well-documented locations for Dahshur town and El Katameya district, not fabricated.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from GEM's own pipeline name (Dahshur, Giza -> New Administrative Capital, Cairo) plus the litigation source's route detail (Cairo/Giza governorates, passing El Katameya) and the egy-map/Presidency source's stated purpose (feeding the New Capital's Siemens power station). No coordinates were invented: Dahshur and El Katameya are well-known named localities; the New Capital endpoint is given only as the general downtown/government-district area since the specific power-plant gate coordinates were not found in any source I could verify. Suggested accuracy raised from 'low' to 'medium' on the strength of one independently-confirmed waypoint (Katameya) and named, governorate-bounded endpoints -- not to 'high' because the precise plant tie-in point and the exact pipe corridor between Dahshur and Katameya remain unsourced.

summary: P3930 confirmed (caveat) -- existence/specs (70km/32in/EGP605M/2017) independently corroborated by 3 sources (Ahram 2017 court case, egy-map/Presidency, petro-news.com survey); NOT a duplicate of P7574 or P3366 despite all three feeding the same New Capital Siemens plant, as the same independent survey lists all three as separate line items with distinct specs; caveats: FuelSource cell wrongly holds a URL instead of 'Natural gas', Operator (GASCO) could be added alongside Owner EGAS, and route corridor upgraded low->medium (Dahshur -> El Katameya waypoint -> New Capital power-plant zone) with the plant's exact tie-in point still unsourced.
